ai.description: This frog reaches 10–12 cm. It features a golden-brown back, dark lateral bands, and a white upper lip. Distinctive traits include a pointed snout and long, slender limbs with extensive toe webbing.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hylarana magna* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent cream-colored dorsolateral fold that extends clearly to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana magna* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high altitudes ranging from 600 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for insects and small invertebrates among the leaf litter and vegetation near forest streams at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana magna* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of eggs in stagnant water bodies or slow-moving streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana magna* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Large Golden-backed Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "chuck" notes, typically heard echoing from near streams within dense tropical forests.
